questions.question: Which figure is associated with the Ninety-Five Theses of 1517?
choices: John Calvin
Thomas More
Martin Luther
Ignatius of Loyola

questions.question: Which practice was a major target of Luther's early criticism?
choices: The sale of indulgences
The election of city councils
The translation of Greek poetry
The collection of customs duties

questions.question: What did indulgences concern in Catholic teaching?
choices: The appointment of hereditary monarchs
The automatic removal of all civil debts
The sale of farmland owned by towns
Remission of temporal punishment for sin

questions.question: Which reformer is especially associated with predestination?
choices: Erasmus
John Calvin
Henry VIII
Johann Gutenberg

questions.question: Which English king broke with papal authority in the 1530s?
choices: Henry VIII
Charles I
James II
William III

questions.question: Which Catholic council clarified doctrine and addressed reform during the sixteenth century?
choices: Council of Nicaea
Council of Constance
Council of Trent
Council of Chalcedon

questions.question: Which religious order founded by Ignatius of Loyola supported Catholic education and missions?
choices: Benedictines
Franciscans
Dominicans
Jesuits

questions.question: How did printing help spread Reformation ideas?
choices: It restricted pamphlets to a single monastery
It allowed arguments and translations to circulate more widely
It prevented religious debates from reaching towns
It made rulers unable to regulate any printed material

questions.question: What did Luther's teaching of justification by faith emphasize?
choices: Salvation through faith rather than earning it through works
Salvation through payment of government taxes
Political loyalty as the sole basis of religious belief
Hereditary rank as the basis for forgiveness

questions.question: Why did some German princes support the Reformation?
choices: It required them to surrender their territories to Spain
It made every prince a pope
It could increase their autonomy and control over church resources
It restored a unified Roman republican government

questions.question: How did vernacular Bible translations affect religious practice?
choices: They ended disagreements about Christian beliefs
They required every reader to learn Latin first
They removed all clergy from European society
They allowed more readers to encounter scripture in familiar languages

questions.question: What did the Peace of Augsburg of 1555 allow within the Holy Roman Empire?
choices: Every subject to freely select any religion without restrictions
Rulers to choose Catholicism or Lutheranism for their territories
The pope to appoint all German princes
Calvinism to become the only permitted religion

questions.question: Why is the English Reformation not explained solely by theology?
choices: Dynastic concerns and royal power also shaped the break with Rome
England had no Christian churches before Henry VIII
Printing was banned throughout the entire period
All English rulers agreed with Luther on every doctrine

questions.question: What distinguishes Anabaptists from groups that practiced infant baptism?
choices: They rejected baptism in every form
They favored baptism following a believer's profession of faith
They required baptism to be performed by a monarch
They limited baptism to hereditary nobles

questions.question: What was a major long-term effect of the Reformation in western Europe?
choices: The disappearance of Christianity
The end of all state involvement in religion
The creation of identical churches in every region
The growth of multiple Christian denominations

questions.question: Which sequence places these Reformation developments correctly?
choices: Peace of Augsburg → Ninety-Five Theses → English break with Rome
English break with Rome → Peace of Augsburg → Ninety-Five Theses
Ninety-Five Theses → English break with Rome → Peace of Augsburg
Ninety-Five Theses → Peace of Augsburg → English break with Rome

questions.question: A prince accepts Lutheranism and takes control of former church lands. What does this example show?
choices: Religious change could be connected to political and economic interests
The Reformation had no effects on governing institutions
Every Protestant movement rejected secular rulers
Catholic rulers had already ended all church property ownership

questions.question: Which evidence most directly challenges the claim that Catholic leaders made no response to Protestant criticism?
choices: The increasing circulation of classical literature in Italian cities
The reforms and doctrinal decisions of the Council of Trent
The growth of Atlantic trade during the sixteenth century
The expansion of universities devoted to secular legal study

questions.question: Why should historians compare Catholic and Protestant accounts of the same religious conflict?
choices: Every religious author had access to the same information
Written accounts cannot be compared with physical evidence
Authors' religious positions could influence how they described events
The most widely circulated account must be the most accurate

questions.question: A student says the Reformation immediately created modern religious freedom throughout Europe. Which correction is best?
choices: All European rulers abandoned religious policies in 1517
The Peace of Augsburg protected every possible belief equally
Religious conflict ended before the Reformation began
Many states continued to enforce an official religion and restrict dissent
